cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Guilin and Yangshuo
tagline: Karst peaks and the Li River, China's classic landscape
summary: Guilin's limestone peaks rising beside the Li River are one of China's most famous views, printed on the 20-yuan note. Cruise the river to Yangshuo, cycle or bamboo-raft through the Yulong valley, explore lit caves and see the Longji rice terraces in the hills to the north.
seasonNote: April to May and September to November are best. Summer is hot with heavy rain that can make the river high. Avoid the October Golden Week crowds.
arrival: Guilin Liangjiang Airport has flights across China. High-speed trains reach Guangzhou in about 2.5 hours and Hong Kong in about 3. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: Taxis and Didi in Guilin; the Li River cruise or a bus links to Yangshuo, where bikes and e-scooters are best.
foodTip: Guilin rice noodles, Yangshuo beer fish and Guangxi river snails (luosifen).
buyTip: Osmanthus tea and wine, and Guilin chilli sauce.
baseArea: Central Guilin near the lakes, or Yangshuo for the countryside

items.name: Li River cruise
items.summary: A four-hour cruise past karst peaks, bamboo groves and water buffalo from Guilin to Yangshuo.
items.expect: Book ahead; the 20-yuan note view is near Xingping.

items.name: Reed Flute Cave
items.summary: A cave of stalactites lit in bright colours, with ancient inscriptions.
items.tip: Look for the Crystal Palace chamber.

items.name: Elephant Trunk Hill
items.summary: A hill shaped like an elephant drinking from the river, the city's symbol.
items.expect: View it free from the opposite bank.
items.tip: See it from the riverbank at dusk.

items.name: Sun and Moon Pagodas
items.summary: Two lakeside pagodas, one copper and one glass, lit up at night.

items.name: Yangshuo and the Yulong River
items.summary: A riverside town among karst peaks, with bamboo rafting and cycling through the Yulong valley.
items.expect: About 1.5 hours by road from Guilin.
items.tip: Cycle to Dragon Bridge and raft back.

items.name: Xianggong Hill
items.summary: A lookout above a great bend in the Li River, famous at sunrise.

items.name: Longji Rice Terraces
items.summary: Mountains carved into rice terraces by Zhuang and Yao villagers over centuries.
items.expect: About 2 hours by road; stay overnight in Ping'an.
items.tip: Visit in late September for golden rice.

items.name: Guilin rice noodles
items.summary: Soft rice noodles with braised meat, peanuts and pickles, eaten for breakfast.
items.tip: Add the house chilli and pickled beans.

items.name: Yangshuo beer fish
items.summary: River carp braised in local beer with tomatoes and peppers.

items.name: Luosifen
items.summary: Guangxi's sour, spicy river-snail rice noodle soup with a strong smell.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Chengdu
tagline: Giant pandas, teahouses and fiery Sichuan food
summary: Sichuan's laid-back capital is the best place in the world to see giant pandas, and one of China's great food cities. Days here mix teahouses in leafy parks, Buddhist temples, old lanes and Sichuan opera, with the Leshan Giant Buddha and Dujiangyan within day-trip range.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are mild. Summer is hot and humid, and winter is damp and grey. Pandas are most active on cool mornings.
arrival: Chengdu has two airports, Tianfu and Shuangliu, both linked by metro. High-speed trains reach Xi'an in about 3.5 hours and Chongqing in about 1.5. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: An extensive metro network, plus taxis and Didi.
foodTip: Hotpot, mapo tofu, dan dan noodles, chuan chuan skewers and rabbit head for the brave.
buyTip: Sichuan peppercorns, Shu embroidery and panda souvenirs.
baseArea: Around Chunxi Road or near Kuanzhai Alley

connections.note: Fast trains through the Qinling mountains.

items.name: Giant Panda Breeding Base
items.wiki: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding
items.summary: Bamboo-filled enclosures where giant and red pandas eat, climb and nap.
items.expect: Arrive at opening; pandas sleep by late morning.
items.tip: Book tickets online and be there by 7:30.
items.why: The best place to see pandas.

items.name: Wenshu Monastery
items.summary: A working Buddhist monastery with gardens, a teahouse and a vegetarian restaurant.
items.tip: Have tea and a vegetarian lunch inside.

items.name: People's Park teahouse
items.summary: Locals drink tea, play mahjong and get their ears cleaned under the trees.
items.expect: Cheap tea; stay as long as you like.

items.name: Kuanzhai Alley
items.summary: Restored Qing-era lanes of courtyards, snacks and teahouses.

items.name: Wuhou Shrine and Jinli Street
items.summary: A shrine to the Three Kingdoms hero Zhuge Liang, beside the lantern-lit Jinli street.
items.expect: Jinli is free; the shrine has a fee.
items.tip: Visit the shrine, then eat on Jinli.

items.name: Sichuan opera face-changing
items.summary: An evening show of opera, puppets, fire-spitting and masks that change in a flash.
items.tip: Book a seat near the front.

items.name: Jinsha Site Museum
items.summary: The remains of a 3,000-year-old Shu kingdom city with gold masks and the Sun Bird.
items.expect: Pair with Sanxingdui for the full story.
items.tip: See the golden Sun and Bird disc.

items.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
items.summary: A 71 m Buddha carved into a cliff in the 8th century, the largest in the world.
items.expect: About an hour by fast train; long queues on the stairs.
items.tip: Take the boat for the full view.

items.name: Dujiangyan irrigation system
items.summary: A 2,000-year-old irrigation system still watering the Sichuan plain.

items.name: Sichuan hotpot
items.summary: A bubbling pot of chilli and Sichuan pepper broth for cooking meat and vegetables.
items.expect: Ask for a split pot if you can't handle the heat.

items.name: Mapo tofu
items.summary: Silky tofu in a numbing, spicy chilli bean sauce, invented in Chengdu.

items.name: Dan dan noodles and chuan chuan
items.summary: Spicy sesame noodles, and skewers you cook in a communal spicy broth.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Hangzhou
tagline: West Lake, tea hills and classic Chinese poetry
summary: Hangzhou's West Lake, ringed by willow-lined causeways, pagodas and misty hills, inspired centuries of Chinese poets and painters. Beyond the lake are the Buddhist caves of Lingyin, the Longjing tea plantations and nearby canal water towns.
seasonNote: Spring blossoms and autumn osmanthus are the highlights. Summer is hot and humid. Weekends and holidays are very crowded at the lake.
arrival: High-speed trains from Shanghai take about an hour. Xiaoshan Airport is about 45 minutes away. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: Metro, buses and public bikes; walking or cycling around West Lake.
foodTip: Dongpo pork, West Lake fish in vinegar sauce, Longjing shrimp and beggar's chicken.
buyTip: Longjing (Dragon Well) tea and Hangzhou silk.
baseArea: Near West Lake's north or east shore

items.name: West Lake
items.summary: A lake of causeways, islands, pagodas and gardens, a World Heritage cultural landscape.
items.expect: Free; rent a bike or take a boat to the islands.
items.tip: Walk the Bai Causeway at sunrise.

items.name: Su Causeway
items.summary: A 3 km willow-lined causeway with six arched bridges across the lake.

items.name: Lingyin Temple
items.summary: One of China's largest Buddhist temples, beside the carved Feilai Feng caves.
items.expect: Busy; separate park and temple tickets.
items.tip: See the laughing Buddha carvings at Feilai Feng.

items.name: Leifeng Pagoda
items.summary: A rebuilt pagoda with lake views and the legend of the White Snake.
items.why: The best view over the lake.

items.name: Longjing tea village
items.summary: Terraced tea plantations where famous Dragon Well green tea is grown.
items.tip: Visit in spring for picking season.

items.name: Hefang Street
items.summary: An old street of traditional shops, medicine halls and snacks.

items.name: Xixi Wetland
items.summary: Wetlands of canals, persimmon trees and old villages explored by electric boat.

items.name: Wuzhen water town
items.summary: A canal town of stone bridges and wooden houses, beautiful when lit at night.
items.tip: Stay overnight in the West Scenic Zone.

items.name: Dongpo pork
items.summary: Slow-braised pork belly in soy and Shaoxing wine, named after the poet Su Dongpo.

items.name: West Lake fish in vinegar sauce
items.wiki: West Lake Fish in Vinegar Gravy
items.summary: Poached grass carp in a sweet-sour vinegar glaze.

items.name: Beggar's chicken and Longjing shrimp
items.summary: Chicken baked in clay and lotus leaves, and river shrimp stir-fried with tea leaves.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Zhangjiajie
tagline: Towering sandstone pillars and glass skywalks
summary: Thousands of sandstone pillars, many draped in pine and mist, rise from the forests of Zhangjiajie in Hunan. The landscape inspired the floating mountains of Avatar. Walk among them in the national park, ride the cliffside Bailong lift, and cross glass bridges and skywalks on Tianmen Mountain.
seasonNote: April to May and September to November are best. Summer is busy and rainy. Winter can be icy but quiet. Avoid Chinese holidays, when queues are very long.
arrival: Zhangjiajie Hehua Airport has flights from major Chinese cities. High-speed trains from Changsha take about 1.5 hours. Wulingyuan, near the park entrance, is about 40 minutes from the city. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: Park shuttle buses and lifts inside the park (included in the multi-day ticket). Taxis and buses between town and the gates.
foodTip: Tujia three-pot stews, smoked pork and spicy Hunan stir-fries.
baseArea: Wulingyuan town near the park gate

items.name: Zhangjiajie National Forest Park
items.summary: China's first national forest park, full of sandstone pillars, streams and cliff trails.
items.expect: The ticket covers four days; allow at least two.
items.tip: Start early to beat tour groups.

items.name: Yuanjiajie and Avatar Hallelujah Mountain
items.summary: The pillar landscape that inspired Avatar, with the First Bridge Under Heaven.

items.name: Bailong Elevator
items.summary: A 326 m glass lift up a cliff face, among the tallest outdoor lifts in the world.
items.tip: Ride it up rather than down.

items.name: Tianzi Mountain
items.summary: High peaks with sweeping views over a sea of pillars, reached by cable car.

items.name: Golden Whip Stream
items.summary: A flat 7 km walk along a stream beneath the pillars, with monkeys.
items.tip: Keep food hidden from the monkeys.

items.name: Tianmen Mountain
items.summary: A long cable car from the city, glass skywalks on the cliffs and a huge natural arch called Heaven's Gate.
items.tip: Ride the cable car up and the bus down the 99-bend road.

items.name: Grand Canyon Glass Bridge
items.summary: A glass-bottomed bridge 300 m above a canyon.

items.name: Tujia three-pot stew
items.summary: Three small pots of tripe, pork and beef simmered with chilli at the table.

items.name: Hunan stir-fries
items.summary: Smoky, hot dishes such as smoked pork with peppers and chopped chilli fish head.
items.expect: Very spicy; ask for less if needed.
items.tip: Try fish head with chopped chilli.

items.name: Stinky tofu
items.summary: Fermented tofu fried black and served with chilli.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Guangzhou
tagline: Canton's great food city on the Pearl River
summary: Guangzhou, old Canton, has been a trading port for 2,000 years and is the home of Cantonese food. Spend mornings at dim sum, wander colonial Shamian Island and the carved Chen Clan hall, and watch the skyline light up from a Pearl River cruise or the Canton Tower.
seasonNote: October to December is sunny and dry. Summer is hot, humid and stormy. Hotels get expensive during the Canton Fair in April and October.
arrival: Baiyun Airport is about 45 minutes by metro. High-speed trains reach Hong Kong West Kowloon in under an hour and Shenzhen in about 30 minutes. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: A huge metro network; taxis and Didi.
foodTip: Dim sum, roast goose, cheung fun rice rolls, wonton noodles and double-skin milk pudding.
buyTip: Tea from Fangcun tea market, and everything at the wholesale markets.

items.name: Canton Tower
items.summary: A 600 m twisted tower with a sky deck and a slow Ferris wheel on top.
items.expect: Expensive at the top; lit beautifully at night.

items.name: Chen Clan Ancestral Hall
items.summary: An 1890s academy covered in wood, stone, brick and ceramic carvings.
items.tip: Look at the roof ridge ceramics.

items.name: Shamian Island
items.summary: A quiet island of colonial-era European buildings under banyan trees.
items.tip: Walk it in the late afternoon.

items.name: Pearl River night cruise
items.summary: An evening boat past the lit skyline and Canton Tower.
items.expect: Board at Tianzi or Xidi piers.
items.tip: Pick a later sailing for full lights.

items.name: Yuexiu Park and the Five Rams
items.summary: A hilly park with the Five Rams statue, city wall and Zhenhai Tower museum.
items.tip: See the Five Rams, the city's legend.

items.name: Nanyue King Mausoleum Museum
items.wiki: Museum of the Mausoleum of the Nanyue King
items.summary: A 2,000-year-old king's tomb with a jade burial suit.
items.expect: One of China's best small museums.

items.name: Temple of the Six Banyan Trees
items.wiki: Temple of the Six Banyan Trees
items.summary: A 1,400-year-old temple with the colourful Flower Pagoda.
items.tip: Look up at the pagoda's painted eaves.

items.name: Shangxiajiu pedestrian street
items.summary: Arcaded shophouse street packed with shops and snacks.

items.name: Dim sum (yum cha)
items.summary: Tea with har gow, siu mai, char siu bao and dozens of small dishes.
items.expect: Best in the morning; traditional teahouses fill early.
items.tip: Tap the table twice to thank the tea pourer.

items.name: Roast goose and char siu
items.summary: Crisp-skinned roast goose and honeyed barbecue pork over rice.
items.expect: Look for meats hanging in the window.

items.name: Cheung fun and double-skin milk
items.summary: Silky steamed rice rolls, then a sweet double-skin milk pudding.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Shenzhen
tagline: China's futuristic tech city next to Hong Kong
summary: A fishing area turned megacity in four decades, Shenzhen is China's tech capital, with gleaming towers, the giant Huaqiangbei electronics market, design districts and long seaside parks. It's an easy add-on from Hong Kong, with beaches and an old fortress town in the east.
seasonNote: October to December is sunny and comfortable. Summer is hot, wet and stormy.
arrival: Cross from Hong Kong at Lo Wu or Futian, or take the high-speed train from West Kowloon (about 20 minutes). Bao'an Airport has flights across China. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: A fast, clean metro; taxis and Didi.
foodTip: Cantonese and Hakka food, Chaoshan beef hotpot and Shajing oysters.
buyTip: Electronics and gadgets at Huaqiangbei; art copies at Dafen.

connections.note: Or the MTR to Lo Wu or Lok Ma Chau and walk across.

items.name: Ping An Finance Centre Free Sky
items.summary: An observation deck on the 116th floor of one of the world's tallest towers.
items.expect: Clear days are best; bring your passport.
items.tip: Go before sunset and stay for the lights.

items.name: Huaqiangbei electronics market
items.summary: Floors of stalls selling every component, phone and gadget imaginable.

items.name: Lianhuashan Park
items.summary: A hill park with a statue of Deng Xiaoping and views over the Futian skyline.

items.name: OCT Loft
items.summary: Old factories turned into galleries, design shops and cafés.

items.name: Dafen Oil Painting Village
items.summary: A village of studios producing a huge share of the world's oil painting copies.

items.name: Shenzhen Bay Park
items.summary: A 15 km seaside promenade facing Hong Kong, with bikes and birdlife.

items.name: Window of the World
items.summary: A theme park of miniature world landmarks, from the Eiffel Tower to the pyramids.
items.tip: Go in the evening for the light show.

items.name: Dapeng Fortress
items.summary: A 600-year-old walled coastal town near the eastern beaches.
items.expect: Combine with Dameisha or Xichong beaches.

items.name: Chaoshan beef hotpot
items.summary: Fresh-cut beef cuts swished in a light broth for seconds.
items.expect: Ask the server how long for each cut.

items.name: Hakka restaurants
items.summary: Salt-baked chicken, stuffed tofu and pork with preserved greens.

items.name: Shajing oysters
items.summary: Grilled oysters with garlic, from the old oyster village of Shajing.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Suzhou
tagline: Classical gardens and canals, the 'Venice of the East'
summary: Suzhou's canals and white-walled houses frame China's finest classical gardens, nine of them World Heritage sites. Explore the Humble Administrator's and Lingering gardens, stroll Pingjiang Road, see I.M. Pei's Suzhou Museum, and visit nearby water towns.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best for gardens. Summer is hot and humid. Gardens get very crowded on holidays.
arrival: High-speed trains from Shanghai take about 30 minutes. Shanghai's airports are 1 to 2 hours away. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules before you go.
gettingAround: Metro, buses, taxis, bikes and canal boats.
foodTip: Squirrel-shaped mandarin fish, Suzhou noodles in clear broth and sweet pastries.
buyTip: Suzhou silk and embroidery, and Biluochun green tea.
baseArea: Inside the old city near Pingjiang Road

items.name: Humble Administrator's Garden
items.summary: The largest classical garden, with ponds, pavilions and zigzag bridges.
items.expect: Very popular; book tickets and go early.

items.name: Lingering Garden
items.summary: A garden of courtyards, carved windows and the tall Cloud-Capped Peak rock.

items.name: Master of the Nets Garden
items.summary: A small, perfect garden with evening opera performances in summer.
items.expect: Night tours in the warm months.

items.name: Suzhou Museum
items.summary: I.M. Pei's modern take on a Suzhou garden, with art and artefacts.
items.tip: Look at the stone-and-water garden wall.

items.name: Pingjiang Road
items.summary: A canal-side lane of teahouses, shops and pingtan storytelling.
items.tip: Listen to pingtan in a teahouse.

items.name: Tiger Hill
items.summary: A hill with a leaning 1,000-year-old pagoda and the Sword Pool legend.

items.name: Zhouzhuang water town
items.summary: A canal town of stone bridges and Ming-era houses, explored by boat.

items.name: Tongli water town
items.summary: A quieter water town with the Retreat and Reflection Garden.

items.name: Squirrel-shaped mandarin fish
items.summary: Mandarin fish scored, fried crisp and glazed in sweet-sour sauce.

items.name: Suzhou noodles
items.summary: Fine noodles in clear broth with toppings like fried fish or braised pork.
items.tip: Order the toppings on the side.

items.name: Suzhou pastries
items.summary: Flaky Suzhou-style mooncakes and sweet sticky rice cakes.
